sources.title: 14.382 Spring 2017 Lecture 8: Linear Panel Data Models Under Strict and Weak Exogeneity
sources.text_scope: Pages 1–2 and 5–10; selected surrounding context. Physical and printed page numbers agree.
verified_scope: Pages 5–6: within transformation, rank and score covariance formed at the unit level; independent units allow within-unit serial dependence.
Page 8: unit-mean correlated-effect construction and FE comparison.
Pages 9–10: dynamic within/first-difference endogeneity, sequential information sets and lagged moments.
equation_cautions: The actual page 9 images contain nonzero signs in both displayed dynamic endogeneity calculations; text extraction lost them. Preserve the signs and supply initial-condition assumptions.

Page 8 displays orthogonality of the heterogeneity residual to the unit mean alone. That restriction alone does not establish orthogonality to every dated regressor. Use a full conditional-mean restriction or restrict the claim to the balanced-sample FE slope identity.
Use explicit conditional expectations rather than allowing the perpendicular symbol to suggest independence.
sources.not_adopted: Empirical examples, a general dynamic bias formula, bootstrap validity and causal validation from nonrejection of a trend test.

sources.title: Econometrics of Cross Section and Panel Data: Lecture 3, Linear Panel Data Models I
sources.type: Author course notes hosted by cemmap/PEPA
sources.text_scope: Physical pages 39–45, Lecture 3 printed pages 1–7. The other lectures in the combined file were not audited.
verified_scope: Printed pages 2–4 distinguish contemporaneous, strict and sequential exogeneity; equation (1.8) states the conditional-mean RE restriction.
Printed page 5 separates full-history linear projection from the unit-mean conditional specification.
Printed pages 6–7 distinguish robust comparison from the usual Hausman covariance-difference calculation and restrict comparison to identified, nonredundant slopes.
equation_cautions: A subsequent conditional-mean conclusion on printed page 5 requires the conditional-mean version, not merely the displayed linear projection. Preserve that distinction.
Printed page 7 says time effects can introduce a 'nonsingularity'; context and redundant comparisons indicate singularity. This wording was checked in the actual page image.
sources.not_adopted: No current Stata behavior claim, automatic robust Hausman chi-square law, unbalanced-panel FE/CRE identity, nonlinear CRE result or unexamined later section.

sources.author: Manuel Arellano
sources.title: Dynamic Panel Data Models II: Lags and Predetermined Variables
sources.type: Author class notes hosted by CEMFI
sources.text_scope: Setup on pages 1–4; pages 9–15. Physical and printed page numbers agree. Application prose supplies context, not validated empirical findings.
verified_scope: Page 10, equations (37)–(40): strict explanatory-variable exogeneity and a sequential dynamic information set are different restrictions; the former alone permits serially correlated disturbances.
Page 14: nonzero transformed score persists with fixed T as the unit count rises.
Page 15, equations (59)–(63): past-information moments after effect removal, identification and unit-level GMM covariance.
Page 12: aggregate shocks can defeat a cross-sectional law of large numbers.
interpretive_limits: The notes' large-T statements require additional limit conditions; a martingale-difference property alone is not a sufficient law-of-large-numbers theorem. Independence of idiosyncratic units is sufficient for a stated cross-sectional route, not necessary in every possible model.
The chapter should prove a bounded fixed-T counterexample and explicit valid lag moments, not import a general Nickell formula or automatic system-GMM moments.
sources.not_adopted: Application estimates, unrestricted large-T consistency, many-instrument asymptotics and unexamined additional level-moment sections.

sources.author: Jeffrey M. Wooldridge
sources.title: Inverse probability weighted estimation for general missing data problems
sources.type: Author working paper from the issuing research institute
sources.text_scope: Population objective and selection setup, pages 4–8; selection-model context on page 9; identification and nuisance-adjusted theorem on pages 10–11. Physical and printed page numbers agree.
verified_scope: Page 6, Assumption 3.1: specified selection probability, positivity and observation requirements.
Page 10, equations (3.5)–(3.6): conditional expectation recovers the population objective; convergence also needs moment and uniformity conditions.
Page 11, Theorem 3.1: estimation of the selection model enters the influence covariance under its stated likelihood and regularity assumptions.
interpretive_limits: The paper covers more than baseline-observed MAR. The proposed chapter uses that narrower sufficient case and does not equate the entire paper's condition with MAR.
Positivity alone does not guarantee finite variance, and fitted weights do not repair selection on unobserved outcomes. The theorem is not a universal estimated-propensity efficiency result.
sources.not_adopted: The later 2007 journal version, generic nuisance estimation, censoring applications and selection-on-unobservables correction are not audited here.

original_proof_blueprint_proposals.proposal: For iid whole-unit vectors and fixed T, define M = I - 11'/T. Prove the LSDV/within identity by projection. Assume E[u_it | X_i, alpha_i] = 0 and positive-definite E[X_i' M X_i]. Derive consistency and the unit-score sandwich using the c01 and c02 finite-dimensional tools; state exactly the moments needed. Show that time-constant regressors vanish and that removing alpha_i does not prove the exogeneity assumption.
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.prerequisite: c01 LLN/CLT and c02 fixed-rank projection plus independent-cluster score covariance.

original_proof_blueprint_proposals.proposal: For positive sigma_u squared, derive compound-covariance quasi-demeaning with theta = 1 - sqrt(sigma_u squared / (sigma_u squared + T sigma_alpha squared)). Separate the effect-regressor orthogonality needed for consistency from covariance restrictions needed for efficiency. For a balanced common-weight regression with sufficient rank, prove the sample equality between the time-varying slope in regression on dated X and unit means and the FE slope, by within/between orthogonality. Interpret mean coefficients only under an explicit heterogeneity restriction; do not identify time-constant effects by within variation.
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.boundary: sigma_alpha squared = 0 gives pooled weighting. The FE limit as its ratio to sigma_u squared diverges is a limiting statement, not an invertible covariance at infinity. No unbalanced or nonlinear equivalence is promised.

original_proof_blueprint_proposals.topic: An exact fixed-T dynamic bias and a valid lag moment
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.proposal: Use y_i0 = 0, alpha_i = 0, y_i1 = u_i1 and y_i2 = rho u_i1 + u_i2 with independent fair signs u and independent units. FE over the two transitions equals rho - 1 + sum_i u_i1 u_i2 / n; thus its probability limit is rho - 1. At rho = 1/2 it converges to -1/2. Extend to y_i3 = rho y_i2 + u_i3: E[y_i1 (u_i3 - u_i2)] = 0 and E[y_i1 Delta y_i2] = rho - 1. The moment is relevant for rho unequal to 1 and loses rank at rho = 1 under this initial law. Prove both calculations from the finite distribution, then form the fixed-dimensional unit moment vector using c03.
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.boundary: This is an original bounded example, not the stationary Nickell bias formula. No serially correlated innovation or different initial condition is silently allowed. Difference errors remain serially dependent.

original_proof_blueprint_proposals.topic: Attrition target, positivity and fitted weights
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.proposal: Let baseline history H be always observed, with finitely many positive-probability cells and P(R = 1 | W, H) = p(H) at least epsilon. Prove E[R psi(W)/p(H)] = E[psi(W)]. With equal-probability H cells, conditional outcome means 2 and 6, and response probabilities 1 and 1/3, the full-population mean is 4 while the respondent mean is 3. Derive the finite-cell estimator and its influence function from the observed cell counts and totals; account for estimated response probabilities rather than reusing an oracle-weight covariance. Construct observationally indistinguishable missing-outcome laws to show the unobserved-selection failure.
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.boundary: For an empty-response cell the finite-sample ratio is undefined; positivity is a population assumption, not a guarantee that every sample cell is nonempty. At population p = 0, unrestricted missing outcomes are not point identified.

original_proof_blueprint_proposals.topic: The sampling unit and common dependence
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.proposal: Treat the unit score as one observation and distinguish fixed T, large n from long T. Construct a common-shock score that survives averaging across units. For u_it = lambda_i F_t + epsilon_it, derive that subtracting each date's cross-sectional mean removes a homogeneous loading but generally leaves (lambda_i - mean lambda) F_t. State a conditional estimand explicitly if conditioning on common shocks. Apply only a proved cluster theorem under its actual independent-unit hypotheses.
original_proof_blueprint_proposals.boundary: No generic two-way-cluster, interactive-factor, spatial, few-cluster or joint large-n/large-T theorem is inherited from c02.

source_questions_and_decisions.authoring_decision: Use the four inspected sources for method scope and limitations. Prefer bounded original counterexamples, explicitly identified moments and fixed-dimensional proofs. Do not present source preparation as a chapter, c04 prerequisite completion or reader acceptance.
